name: SawariGo
tagline: Cabs and autos in 25 cities, where New Year's Eve ends the year with its busiest hour
summary: SawariGo matches riders with 3 lakh cab and auto drivers: rider and driver apps, matching, fares and surge, maps, trips, payments, SOS safety and notifications. On New Year's Eve demand climbs all evening and peaks at eight times a normal busy hour just before midnight. Riders stuck on 'searching for drivers', fares that change after the quote and late SOS alerts keep coming back.

tour.headline: Matching searches every driver in the city for every ride request, so every busy night leaves riders searching; a geospatial index costs 12 hours.

incidents.title: Riders stuck on 'searching for drivers' for 15 minutes
incidents.desc: On Saturday night riders in Bengaluru saw 'searching for drivers' for up to 15 minutes while drivers were nearby.
whys: Matching took over 15 minutes
Each match request scanned every online driver in the city
Matching searches every driver in the city instead of nearby cells
incidents.fix: Limited the search radius to 3 km.
incidents.lesson: A radius cut hides drivers just outside it.

incidents.title: Driver locations frozen on the rider's map
incidents.desc: Riders saw their driver's car stuck on the map for 10 minutes while the driver was moving.
whys: Riders saw drivers stuck in place
Location pings queued behind slow database writes
Driver location pings are written to the main database every 3 seconds
incidents.lesson: Dropping pings is not the same as keeping up.

incidents.title: Fare jumped from Rs 240 to Rs 410 between quote and booking
incidents.desc: Riders were shown one fare and charged a much higher one because surge changed while they booked.
whys: Riders were charged more than the quote
Surge was recalculated at booking time
Surge is recalculated at booking instead of honouring the quoted fare
incidents.fix: Refunded the difference to complaining riders.
incidents.lesson: Only the riders who complained got refunds.

incidents.title: Two riders assigned the same driver
incidents.desc: A driver received two ride requests at once and accepted both; one rider waited 20 minutes and cancelled.
whys: A driver received two rides at once
Two matches read the driver as free at the same time
Driver assignment has no lock on the driver's state
incidents.lesson: The race returns whenever demand spikes.

incidents.title: Wallet debited but trip shows unpaid
incidents.desc: Riders paid from the wallet but drivers saw the trip as unpaid and asked for cash.
whys: Riders were asked to pay cash after a wallet debit
The wallet callback failed after the debit
Wallet debits are not reconciled with completed trips
incidents.fix: Refunded double payments from a report.
incidents.lesson: Drivers and riders both lost trust.

incidents.title: SOS alert reached the emergency contact 9 minutes late
incidents.desc: A rider pressed SOS at 23:40; the SMS to her emergency contact arrived 9 minutes later.
whys: An SOS SMS was delayed
SOS messages waited behind a promotional campaign
SOS alerts share a queue with promotional notifications
incidents.lesson: Safety cannot depend on the marketing calendar.

incidents.title: Trip status updates delayed during Diwali night
incidents.desc: Trips stayed 'driver arriving' after drivers had arrived because status writes waited for database connections.
whys: Trips stayed 'arriving' after drivers arrived
Trip updates waited for database connections used by location writes
Driver location pings are written to the main database every 3 seconds

incidents.title: Ride-start OTP rejected as expired at midnight
incidents.desc: Drivers could not start rides between 00:00 and 00:15 because valid OTPs were rejected as expired.
whys: Drivers could not start rides
OTP expiry was computed in UTC and crossed the day boundary
Trip OTP expiry uses the server's UTC clock
incidents.fix: Allowed drivers to skip the OTP.
incidents.lesson: Skipping the OTP removes a safety check.

incidents.title: Matching timeouts across Bengaluru at 22:30
incidents.desc: After a concert ended, match requests timed out across the city for 12 minutes.
whys: Match requests timed out
Every request scanned all online drivers again
Matching searches every driver in the city instead of nearby cells
incidents.lesson: The scan grows with drivers and riders together.

incidents.title: Quoted fare not honoured on New Year's morning
incidents.desc: Riders booking at 00:30 on New Year's morning were charged up to 70% above their quote.
whys: Riders paid more than their quote
Surge changed between quote and booking
Surge is recalculated at booking instead of honouring the quoted fare

incidents.title: Driver app shows the wrong location for 10 minutes
incidents.desc: Drivers' positions lagged 10 minutes behind during the cricket final.
whys: Driver positions lagged
Location writes backed up in the main database
Driver location pings are written to the main database every 3 seconds
incidents.fix: Sent pings every 10 seconds instead of 3.
incidents.lesson: Less frequent pings make ETAs worse.

incidents.title: UPI payment marked failed though the rider was debited
incidents.desc: UPI payments succeeded at the bank but trips were marked unpaid for 400 rides.
whys: Paid trips were marked unpaid
The bank's confirmation reached us after the trip closed
Wallet debits are not reconciled with completed trips
incidents.fix: Marked the trips paid from the bank report.
incidents.lesson: Again found by drivers, not by us.

incidents.title: Pickup ETA off by 20 minutes on flyovers
incidents.desc: Pickups near flyovers were routed under the flyover and back, and ETAs were 20 minutes wrong.
whys: Pickup ETAs were wrong
Routing treated flyovers and the roads below as connected
The road graph has no levels for flyovers and underpasses
incidents.fix: Blocked the worst junctions by hand.

incidents.title: Driver received two simultaneous ride requests
incidents.desc: Drivers again got two rides at once during the evening peak; both riders were left waiting.
whys: A driver was assigned two rides
Two matching workers saw the driver as available
Driver assignment has no lock on the driver's state
incidents.lesson: Busy nights make the race likely.

incidents.title: SOS alert delayed during a festival campaign
incidents.desc: An SOS alert took 6 minutes to reach the emergency contact during a festival promotion.
whys: The SOS SMS was delayed
SOS messages queued behind festival promotions
SOS alerts share a queue with promotional notifications
incidents.lesson: This must never happen a third time.

incidents.title: Main database at 100% during the cricket final
incidents.desc: All services slowed for 20 minutes as location writes saturated the main database.
whys: All services slowed
Location writes saturated the database
Driver location pings are written to the main database every 3 seconds
incidents.fix: Moved to a bigger database instance.
incidents.lesson: Bigger hardware for the same writes.

incidents.title: Ride OTP failing just after midnight
incidents.desc: Drivers could not start rides for 15 minutes after midnight because OTPs looked expired.
whys: Ride OTPs were rejected after midnight
Expiry used UTC and the date changed
Trip OTP expiry uses the server's UTC clock
incidents.fix: Let drivers skip the OTP again.

incidents.title: Riders charged more than the quoted fare
incidents.desc: Riders were charged above their quoted fare during last night's rain surge.
whys: Riders paid more than quoted
Surge was recalculated while they booked
Surge is recalculated at booking instead of honouring the quoted fare

incidents.title: Driver-arrived notifications 5 minutes late
incidents.desc: Riders got 'Your driver has arrived' 5 minutes after the driver arrived.
whys: Notifications were late
Notifications are sent inline from the trip service
Trip notifications are sent synchronously without a queue

incidents.title: Riders waiting 20 minutes for a match across the city
incidents.desc: Since 22:00 riders across Bengaluru and Pune are waiting up to 20 minutes for a match.
whys: Riders wait 20 minutes for a match
Each request scans every online driver
Matching searches every driver in the city instead of nearby cells

debts.title: Geospatial index of drivers by map cell
debts.desc: Index online drivers by map cell and search only the rider's cell and its neighbours, instead of a full table scan of every online driver.
debts.cause: Matching searches every driver in the city instead of nearby cells

debts.title: Keep live driver locations in memory and batch writes to the database
debts.desc: Hold the latest location of each driver in an in-memory store and save trip trails with batch writes once a minute.
debts.cause: Driver location pings are written to the main database every 3 seconds

debts.title: Fare holds: honour the quoted fare for two minutes
debts.desc: A quote reserves its fare for two minutes; booking within that time uses the held fare even if surge changes.
debts.cause: Surge is recalculated at booking instead of honouring the quoted fare

debts.title: Lock the driver's state when assigning a ride
debts.desc: Assign a driver with a row-level lock on the driver's state so two concurrent matches cannot both take the same driver.
debts.cause: Driver assignment has no lock on the driver's state

debts.title: Reconcile wallet and UPI debits with completed trips every hour
debts.desc: Match every wallet and UPI debit with a completed trip and fix any trip marked unpaid.
debts.cause: Wallet debits are not reconciled with completed trips

debts.title: Dedicated priority queue for SOS alerts
debts.desc: SOS alerts go through their own durable queue and SMS route, never behind promotional messages, with delivery tracked to the second.
debts.cause: SOS alerts share a queue with promotional notifications

debts.title: Use IST and a monotonic clock for ride OTP expiry
debts.desc: Compute OTP expiry from a monotonic clock and show times in IST, so midnight and the date change do not matter.
debts.cause: Trip OTP expiry uses the server's UTC clock

debts.title: Structured road levels for flyovers in the map data
debts.desc: Add structured level data to the road graph so routing never joins a flyover to the road below.
debts.cause: The road graph has no levels for flyovers and underpasses

debts.title: Send trip notifications through a durable queue
debts.desc: Trip milestones publish to a durable queue; workers send push and SMS without slowing the trip service.
debts.cause: Trip notifications are sent synchronously without a queue

debts.title: Separate connection pools for trips and location writes
debts.desc: Location writes and nightly batch jobs get their own pools so they can never starve trip updates.

debts.title: Serve cached fare estimates per route for 60 seconds
debts.desc: Cache fare estimates per pickup cell and destination cell for a minute instead of recomputing for every app refresh.

debts.title: Load test New Year's Eve at 8x
debts.desc: Replay a New Year's Eve evening at 8 times a normal busy hour against staging every December.

debts.title: Retry rider app requests with backoff and jitter
debts.desc: The rider app retries failed requests with exponential backoff and jitter.

spike.name: New Year's Eve
spike.description: Demand climbs from the evening, doubles by 21:00 and peaks at eight times a normal busy hour between 23:00 and midnight as parties end and everyone books at once.
